passages.text: Concerning the Ammonites, this is what the LORD says: “Has Israel no sons? Is he without heir? Why then has Milcom taken possession of Gad? Why have his people settled in their cities?
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks about the Ammonites.
The LORD asks a question.
He says, “Does Israel have no sons?
Does Israel have no heir?
Why has Milcom taken the land of Gad?
Why do Milcom’s people live in Gad’s cities?”
passages.original: לִבְנֵ֣י עַמּ֗וֹן כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הֲבָנִ֥ים אֵין֙ לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אִם־ יוֹרֵ֖שׁ אֵ֣ין ל֑וֹ מַדּ֗וּעַ יָרַ֤שׁ מַלְכָּם֙ אֶת־ גָּ֔ד וְעַמּ֖וֹ בְּעָרָ֥יו יָשָֽׁב׃

passages.text: Therefore, behold, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will sound the battle cry against Rabbah of the Ammonites. It will become a heap of ruins, and its villages will be burned. Then Israel will drive out their dispossessors, says the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks with authority.
The LORD says the days are coming.
The LORD will sound a battle cry against Rabbah.
Rabbah is the main city of the Ammonites.
Rabbah will become a heap of ruins.
The villages around Rabbah will burn with fire.
Israel will drive out those who took their land.
The LORD has declared this.
passages.original: לָכֵ֡ן הִנֵּה֩ יָמִ֨ים בָּאִ֜ים נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֗ה וְ֠הִשְׁמַעְתִּי אֶל־ רַבַּ֨ת בְּנֵי־ עַמּ֜וֹן תְּרוּעַ֣ת מִלְחָמָ֗ה וְהָֽיְתָה֙ לְתֵ֣ל שְׁמָמָ֔ה וּבְנֹתֶ֖יהָ בָּאֵ֣שׁ תִּצַּ֑תְנָה וְיָרַ֧שׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל אֶת־ יֹרְשָׁ֖יו אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Wail, O Heshbon, for Ai has been destroyed; cry out, O daughters of Rabbah! Put on sackcloth and mourn; run back and forth within your walls, for Milcom will go into exile together with his priests and officials.
passages.sermon:
Heshbon, you must wail.
Ai has been destroyed.
Daughters of Rabbah, you must cry out.
Put on sackcloth.
Mourn.
Run back and forth inside your walls.
Milcom will go into exile.
His priests and officials will go with him.
passages.original: הֵילִ֨ילִי חֶשְׁבּ֜וֹן כִּ֣י שֻׁדְּדָה־ עַ֗י צְעַקְנָה֮ בְּנ֣וֹת רַבָּה֒ חֲגֹ֣רְנָה שַׂקִּ֔ים סְפֹ֕דְנָה וְהִתְשׁוֹטַ֖טְנָה בַּגְּדֵר֑וֹת כִּ֤י מַלְכָּם֙ בַּגּוֹלָ֣ה יֵלֵ֔ךְ כֹּהֲנָ֥יו וְשָׂרָ֖יו יַחְדָּֽיו׃

passages.text: Why do you boast of your valleys— your valleys so fruitful, O faithless daughter? You trust in your riches and say, ‘Who can come against me?’
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the Ammonites.
The Ammonites are called a faithless daughter.
The Ammonites live in fruitful valleys.
The Ammonites boast about their valleys.
The Ammonites trust in their riches.
The Ammonites say, “Who can come against me?”
passages.original: מַה־ תִּתְהַֽלְלִי֙ בָּֽעֲמָקִ֔ים זָ֣ב עִמְקֵ֔ךְ הַבַּ֖ת הַשּֽׁוֹבֵבָ֑ה הַבֹּֽטְחָה֙ בְּאֹ֣צְרֹתֶ֔יהָ מִ֖י יָב֥וֹא אֵלָֽי׃

passages.text: Behold, I am about to bring terror upon you, declares the Lord GOD of Hosts, from all those around you. You will each be driven headlong, with no one to regather the fugitives.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD of Hosts speaks.
He says, “I am about to bring terror upon you.
This terror will come from all those around you.
Each of you will be driven away in panic.
No one will gather those who flee.
No one will bring back the fugitives.
passages.original: הִנְנִי֩ מֵבִ֨יא עָלַ֜יִךְ פַּ֗חַד נְאֻם־ אֲדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה צְבָא֖וֹת מִכָּל־ סְבִיבָ֑יִךְ וְנִדַּחְתֶּם֙ אִ֣ישׁ לְפָנָ֔יו וְאֵ֥ין מְקַבֵּ֖ץ לַנֹּדֵֽד׃

passages.text: Yet afterward I will restore the Ammonites from captivity,” declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD promises restoration.
The LORD will restore the Ammonites.
The Ammonites will return from captivity.
This will happen after their punishment.
passages.original: וְאַחֲרֵי־ כֵ֗ן אָשִׁ֛יב אֶת־ שְׁב֥וּת בְּנֵֽי־ עַמּ֖וֹן נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃ס

passages.text: Concerning Edom, this is what the LORD of Hosts says: “Is there no longer wisdom in Teman? Has counsel perished from the prudent? Has their wisdom decayed?
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts speaks about Edom.
The LORD of Hosts asks about Teman.
He asks if wisdom still exists in Teman.
He asks if the prudent have lost their counsel.
He asks if their wisdom has decayed.
passages.original: לֶאֱד֗וֹם כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת הַאֵ֥ין ע֛וֹד חָכְמָ֖ה בְּתֵימָ֑ן אָבְדָ֤ה עֵצָה֙ מִבָּנִ֔ים נִסְרְחָ֖ה חָכְמָתָֽם׃

passages.text: Turn and run! Lie low, O dwellers of Dedan, for I will bring disaster on Esau at the time I punish him.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people living in Dedan.
God tells them to run away quickly.
God tells them to hide and stay low.
God says He will bring disaster on Esau.
God will punish Esau at the time He has chosen.
passages.original: נֻ֤סוּ הָפְנוּ֙ הֶעְמִ֣יקוּ לָשֶׁ֔בֶת יֹשְׁבֵ֖י דְּדָ֑ן כִּ֣י אֵ֥יד עֵשָׂ֛ו הֵבֵ֥אתִי עָלָ֖יו עֵ֥ת פְּקַדְתִּֽיו׃

passages.text: If grape gatherers came to you, would they not leave some gleanings? Were thieves to come in the night, would they not steal only what they wanted?
passages.sermon:
Grape gatherers come to a vineyard.
They do not take every grape.
They leave some grapes behind.
Thieves come at night.
They steal only what they want.
They do not take everything.
passages.original: אִם־ בֹּֽצְרִים֙ בָּ֣אוּ לָ֔ךְ לֹ֥א יַשְׁאִ֖רוּ עֽוֹלֵל֑וֹת אִם־ גַּנָּבִ֥ים בַּלַּ֖יְלָה הִשְׁחִ֥יתוּ דַיָּֽם׃

passages.text: But I will strip Esau bare; I will uncover his hiding places, and he will be unable to conceal himself. His descendants will be destroyed along with his relatives and neighbors, and he will be no more.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks about Esau.
The LORD says, “I will strip Esau bare.
I will uncover all his hiding places.
Esau will not be able to hide.
I will destroy Esau’s descendants.
I will destroy his relatives.
I will destroy his neighbors.
Esau will be gone.”
passages.original: כִּֽי־ אֲנִ֞י חָשַׂ֣פְתִּי אֶת־ עֵשָׂ֗ו גִּלֵּ֙יתִי֙ אֶת־ מִסְתָּרָ֔יו וְנֶחְבָּ֖ה לֹ֣א יוּכָ֑ל שֻׁדַּ֥ד זַרְע֛וֹ וְאֶחָ֥יו וּשְׁכֵנָ֖יו וְאֵינֶֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: Abandon your orphans; I will preserve their lives. Let your widows trust in Me.”
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Edom.
God commands them to leave their orphans.
God promises to keep the orphans alive.
God tells the widows to trust in Him.
passages.original: עָזְבָ֥ה יְתֹמֶ֖יךָ אֲנִ֣י אֲחַיֶּ֑ה וְאַלְמְנֹתֶ֖יךָ עָלַ֥י תִּבְטָֽחוּ׃ס

passages.text: For this is what the LORD says: “If those who do not deserve to drink the cup must drink it, can you possibly remain unpunished? You will not go unpunished, for you must drink it too.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks with authority.
The LORD says this message.
Some people do not deserve punishment.
These people must still drink the cup of suffering.
You are guilty.
You cannot escape punishment.
You will not go unpunished.
You must also drink the cup of suffering.
passages.original: כִּי־ כֹ֣ה׀ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה הִ֠נֵּה אֲשֶׁר־ אֵ֨ין מִשְׁפָּטָ֜ם לִשְׁתּ֤וֹת הַכּוֹס֙ שָׁת֣וֹ יִשְׁתּ֔וּ וְאַתָּ֣ה ה֔וּא נָקֹ֖ה תִּנָּקֶ֑ה לֹ֣א תִנָּקֶ֔ה כִּ֥י שָׁתֹ֖ה תִּשְׁתֶּֽה׃

passages.text: For by Myself I have sworn, declares the LORD, that Bozrah will become a desolation, a disgrace, a ruin, and a curse, and all her cities will be in ruins forever.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD speaks with authority.
The LORD makes a solemn promise by Himself.
The LORD declares this message.
Bozrah is a city in Edom.
Bozrah will become empty and ruined.
Bozrah will be a place of shame.
Bozrah will be destroyed.
Bozrah will be cursed.
All the cities of Bozrah will become ruins.
These ruins will last forever.
passages.original: כִּ֣י בִ֤י נִשְׁבַּ֙עְתִּי֙ נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֔ה כִּֽי־ לְשַׁמָּ֧ה לְחֶרְפָּ֛ה לְחֹ֥רֶב וְלִקְלָלָ֖ה תִּֽהְיֶ֣ה בָצְרָ֑ה וְכָל־ עָרֶ֥יהָ תִהְיֶ֖ינָה לְחָרְב֥וֹת עוֹלָֽם׃

passages.text: I have heard a message from the LORD; an envoy has been sent to the nations: “Assemble yourselves to march against her! Rise up for battle!”
passages.sermon:
The LORD gave me a message.
I heard this message from the LORD.
The LORD sent an envoy to the nations.
The envoy gave a command to the nations.
The command said, "Gather together.
Come against her.
Get up and prepare for battle."
passages.original: שְׁמוּעָ֤ה שָׁמַ֙עְתִּי֙ מֵאֵ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה וְצִ֖יר בַּגּוֹיִ֣ם שָׁל֑וּחַ הִֽתְקַבְּצוּ֙ וּבֹ֣אוּ עָלֶ֔יהָ וְק֖וּמוּ לַמִּלְחָמָֽה׃

passages.text: “For behold, I will make you small among nations, despised among men.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is speaking.
The LORD has power and authority.
The LORD says, “I will make you small among the nations.
You will be despised among men.
You will not have honor or respect.
You will be looked down upon by others.
You will not be great or important among the nations.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ הִנֵּ֥ה קָטֹ֛ן נְתַתִּ֖יךָ בַּגּוֹיִ֑ם בָּז֖וּי בָּאָדָֽם׃

passages.text: The terror you cause and the pride of your heart have deceived you, O dwellers in the clefts of the rocks, O occupiers of the mountain summit. Though you elevate your nest like the eagle, even from there I will bring you down,” declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to the people of Edom.
You live in the clefts of the rocks.
You make your home on the heights of the mountains.
You cause terror to others.
You have pride in your heart.
Your pride has deceived you.
You build your nest high, like the eagle.
You think you are safe in your high place.
But I, the LORD, will bring you down from there.
I declare this.
passages.original: תִּֽפְלַצְתְּךָ֞ הִשִּׁ֤יא אֹתָךְ֙ זְד֣וֹן לִבֶּ֔ךָ שֹֽׁכְנִי֙ בְּחַגְוֵ֣י הַסֶּ֔לַע תֹּפְשִׂ֖י מְר֣וֹם גִּבְעָ֑ה כִּֽי־ תַגְבִּ֤יהַ כַּנֶּ֙שֶׁר֙ קִנֶּ֔ךָ מִשָּׁ֥ם אֽוֹרִידְךָ֖ נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: “Edom will become an object of horror. All who pass by will be appalled and will scoff at all her wounds.
passages.sermon:
Edom will become a place of horror.
Everyone who passes by Edom will be shocked.
They will see Edom’s wounds.
They will mock Edom because of her wounds.
passages.original: וְהָיְתָ֥ה אֱד֖וֹם לְשַׁמָּ֑ה כֹּ֚ל עֹבֵ֣ר עָלֶ֔יהָ יִשֹּׁ֥ם וְיִשְׁרֹ֖ק עַל־ כָּל־ מַכּוֹתֶֽהָ׃

passages.text: As Sodom and Gomorrah were overthrown along with their neighbors,” says the LORD, “no one will dwell there; no man will abide there.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks with authority.
The LORD destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah.
The LORD also destroyed their neighboring cities.
The LORD says this about Edom.
No one will live there.
No person will stay there.
passages.original: כְּֽמַהְפֵּכַ֞ת סְדֹ֧ם וַעֲמֹרָ֛ה וּשְׁכֵנֶ֖יהָ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה לֹֽא־ יֵשֵׁ֥ב שָׁם֙ אִ֔ישׁ וְלֹֽא־ יָג֥וּר בָּ֖הּ בֶּן־ אָדָֽם׃

passages.text: Behold, one will come up like a lion from the thickets of the Jordan to the watered pasture. For in an instant I will chase Edom from her land. Who is the chosen one I will appoint for this? For who is like Me, and who can challenge Me? What shepherd can stand against Me?”
passages.sermon:
God speaks with power and authority.
God compares His coming judgment to a lion.
A lion rises from the thick bushes by the Jordan River.
The lion moves toward a safe and fertile pasture.
God says He will quickly drive Edom out of her land.
God asks, “Who is the chosen one I will appoint for this?”
God declares, “No one is like Me.”
God asks, “Who can challenge Me?”
God asks, “What shepherd can stand before Me?”
passages.original: הִ֠נֵּה כְּאַרְיֵ֞ה יַעֲלֶ֨ה מִגְּא֣וֹן הַיַּרְדֵּן֮ אֶל־ נְוֵ֣ה אֵיתָן֒ כִּֽי־ אַרְגִּ֤יעָה אֲרִיצֶ֨נּוּ מֵֽעָלֶ֔יהָ וּמִ֥י בָח֖וּר אֵלֶ֣יהָ אֶפְקֹ֑ד כִּ֣י מִ֤י כָמ֙וֹנִי֙ וּמִ֣י יֹעִידֶ֔נִּי וּמִי־ זֶ֣ה רֹעֶ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַעֲמֹ֖ד לְפָנָֽי׃ס

passages.text: Therefore hear the plans that the LORD has drawn up against Edom and the strategies He has devised against the people of Teman: Surely the little ones of the flock will be dragged away; certainly their pasture will be made desolate because of them.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is speaking.
The LORD has made plans against Edom.
The LORD has devised strategies against the people of Teman.
Listen to these plans.
The weakest ones in the flock will be dragged away.
Their pasture will become desolate because of them.
passages.original: לָכֵ֞ן שִׁמְע֣וּ עֲצַת־ יְהוָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר יָעַץ֙ אֶל־ אֱד֔וֹם וּמַ֨חְשְׁבוֹתָ֔יו אֲשֶׁ֥ר חָשַׁ֖ב אֶל־ יֹשְׁבֵ֣י תֵימָ֑ן אִם־ לֹ֤א יִסְחָבוּם֙ צְעִירֵ֣י הַצֹּ֔אן אִם־ לֹ֥א יַשִּׁ֛ים עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם נְוֵהֶֽם׃

passages.text: At the sound of their fall the earth will quake; their cry will resound to the Red Sea.
passages.sermon:
The people of Edom will fall.
The earth will shake when they fall.
Their cry will be loud.
People will hear their cry all the way to the Red Sea.
passages.original: מִקּ֣וֹל נִפְלָ֔ם רָעֲשָׁ֖ה הָאָ֑רֶץ צְעָקָ֕ה בְּיַם־ ס֖וּף נִשְׁמַ֥ע קוֹלָֽהּ׃

passages.text: Look! An eagle will soar and swoop down, spreading its wings over Bozrah. In that day the hearts of Edom’s mighty men will be like the heart of a woman in labor.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about Edom.
Edom is a nation.
God describes what will happen to Edom.
An eagle will rise up.
The eagle will fly high.
The eagle will swoop down.
The eagle will spread its wings over Bozrah.
Bozrah is a city in Edom.
On that day, Edom’s strongest men will be afraid.
Their hearts will be full of fear.
Their fear will be like the fear of a woman in labor.
passages.original: הִנֵּ֤ה כַנֶּ֙שֶׁר֙ יַעֲלֶ֣ה וְיִדְאֶ֔ה וְיִפְרֹ֥שׂ כְּנָפָ֖יו עַל־ בָּצְרָ֑ה וְֽ֠הָיָה לֵ֞ב גִּבּוֹרֵ֤י אֱדוֹם֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא כְּלֵ֖ב אִשָּׁ֥ה מְצֵרָֽה׃ס

passages.text: Concerning Damascus: “Hamath and Arpad are put to shame, for they have heard a bad report; they are agitated like the sea; their anxiety cannot be calmed.
passages.sermon:
This message concerns Damascus.
Hamath and Arpad are two cities.
Hamath and Arpad feel shame.
They heard a bad report.
This report caused them distress.
They are agitated like the sea.
Their anxiety is strong.
They cannot find calm.
passages.original: לְדַמֶּ֗שֶׂק בּ֤וֹשָֽׁה חֲמָת֙ וְאַרְפָּ֔ד כִּי־ שְׁמֻעָ֥ה רָעָ֛ה שָׁמְע֖וּ נָמֹ֑גוּ בַּיָּ֣ם דְּאָגָ֔ה הַשְׁקֵ֖ט לֹ֥א יוּכָֽל׃

passages.text: Damascus has become feeble; she has turned to flee. Panic has gripped her; anguish and pain have seized her like a woman in labor.
passages.sermon:
Damascus is a city.
Damascus has become weak.
Damascus has turned to run away.
Panic has taken hold of Damascus.
Anguish has seized Damascus.
Pain has seized Damascus.
Damascus suffers like a woman in labor.
passages.original: רָפְתָ֥ה דַמֶּ֛שֶׂק הִפְנְתָ֥ה לָנ֖וּס וְרֶ֣טֶט׀ הֶחֱזִ֑יקָה צָרָ֧ה וַחֲבָלִ֛ים אֲחָזַ֖תָּה כַּיּוֹלֵדָֽה׃

passages.text: How is the city of praise not forsaken, the town that brings Me joy?
passages.sermon:
The Lord speaks about Damascus.
Damascus is called the city of praise.
This city brings joy to the Lord.
The Lord asks a question.
He asks why this city is not abandoned.
He wonders how the city of praise is not forsaken.
He calls it the town that brings Him joy.
passages.original: אֵ֥יךְ לֹֽא־ עֻזְּבָ֖ה עִ֣יר תְּהִלָּה קִרְיַ֖ת מְשׂוֹשִֽׂי׃

passages.text: For her young men will fall in the streets, and all her warriors will be silenced in that day,” declares the LORD of Hosts.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts speaks.
He declares what will happen to Damascus.
Her young men will fall in the streets.
All her warriors will be silenced on that day.
passages.original: לָכֵ֛ן יִפְּל֥וּ בַחוּרֶ֖יהָ בִּרְחֹבֹתֶ֑יהָ וְכָל־ אַנְשֵׁ֨י הַמִּלְחָמָ֤ה יִדַּ֙מּוּ֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃

passages.text: “I will set fire to the walls of Damascus; it will consume the fortresses of Ben-hadad.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks with authority.
The LORD says, “I will set fire to the walls of Damascus.
The fire will burn the walls.
The fire will destroy the fortresses of Ben-hadad.
The fortresses will be consumed.”
passages.original: וְהִצַּ֥תִּי אֵ֖שׁ בְּחוֹמַ֣ת דַּמָּ֑שֶׂק וְאָכְלָ֖ה אַרְמְנ֥וֹת בֶּן־ הֲדָֽד׃ס

passages.text: Concerning Kedar and the kingdoms of Hazor, which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon defeated, this is what the LORD says: “Rise up, advance against Kedar, and destroy the people of the east!
passages.sermon:
Nebuchadnezzar was the king of Babylon.
He defeated Kedar and the kingdoms of Hazor.
The LORD speaks about Kedar and Hazor.
The LORD says this:
“Rise up.
Go against Kedar.
Destroy the people of the east.”
passages.original: לְקֵדָ֣ר׀ וּֽלְמַמְלְכ֣וֹת חָצ֗וֹר אֲשֶׁ֤ר הִכָּה֙ נְבוּכַדְרֶאצּוֹר מֶֽלֶךְ־ בָּבֶ֔ל כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה ק֚וּמוּ עֲל֣וּ אֶל־ קֵדָ֔ר וְשָׁדְד֖וּ אֶת־ בְּנֵי־ קֶֽדֶם׃

passages.text: They will take their tents and flocks, their tent curtains and all their goods. They will take their camels for themselves. They will shout to them: ‘Terror is on every side!’
passages.sermon:
Babylon attacked Kedar and the kingdoms of Hazor.
Babylon took action because God commanded them.
Babylon’s soldiers took the tents of the people.
They took the flocks of the people.
They took the tent curtains.
They took all the goods.
They took the camels for themselves.
They shouted to the people.
They said, “Terror is on every side!”
passages.original: אָהֳלֵיהֶ֤ם וְצֹאנָם֙ יִקָּ֔חוּ יְרִיעוֹתֵיהֶ֧ם וְכָל־ כְּלֵיהֶ֛ם וּגְמַלֵּיהֶ֖ם יִשְׂא֣וּ לָהֶ֑ם וְקָרְא֧וּ עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם מָג֖וֹר מִסָּבִֽיב׃

passages.text: Run! Escape quickly! Lie low, O residents of Hazor,” declares the LORD, “for Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has drawn up a plan against you; he has devised a strategy against you.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to the people who live in Hazor.
He says, "Run away.
Escape quickly.
Hide yourselves well.
Nebuchadnezzar is the king of Babylon.
He has made a plan against you.
He has thought of a strategy to harm you."
passages.original: נֻסוּ֩ נֻּ֨דוּ מְאֹ֜ד הֶעְמִ֧יקוּ לָשֶׁ֛בֶת יֹשְׁבֵ֥י חָצ֖וֹר נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֑ה כִּֽי־ יָעַ֨ץ עֲלֵיכֶ֜ם נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֤ר מֶֽלֶךְ־ בָּבֶל֙ עֵצָ֔ה וְחָשַׁ֥ב עֲלֵיהֶם מַחֲשָׁבָֽה׃

passages.text: Rise up, advance against a nation at ease, one that dwells securely,” declares the LORD. “They have no gates or bars; they live alone.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD commands action.
He says, "Rise up.
Go against a nation that is at ease.
This nation lives in safety.
They have no gates.
They have no bars.
They live alone."
passages.original: ק֣וּמוּ עֲל֗וּ אֶל־ גּ֥וֹי שְׁלֵ֛יו יוֹשֵׁ֥ב לָבֶ֖טַח נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֑ה לֹא־ דְלָתַ֧יִם וְלֹֽא־ בְרִ֛יחַ ל֖וֹ בָּדָ֥ד יִשְׁכֹּֽנוּ׃

passages.text: Their camels will become plunder, and their large herds will be spoil. I will scatter to the wind in every direction those who shave their temples; I will bring calamity on them from all sides,” declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD says what will happen to the people of Hazor.
Their enemies will take their camels.
Their enemies will steal their large herds.
The LORD will scatter the people who shave their temples.
The LORD will send them in every direction, like the wind scatters things.
The LORD will bring disaster on them from every side.
passages.original: וְהָי֨וּ גְמַלֵּיהֶ֜ם לָבַ֗ז וַהֲמ֤וֹן מִקְנֵיהֶם֙ לְשָׁלָ֔ל וְזֵרִתִ֥ים לְכָל־ ר֖וּחַ קְצוּצֵ֣י פֵאָ֑ה וּמִכָּל־ עֲבָרָ֛יו אָבִ֥יא אֶת־ אֵידָ֖ם נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: “Hazor will become a haunt for jackals, a desolation forever. No one will dwell there; no man will abide there.”
passages.sermon:
Hazor is a city.
Hazor will become a place for jackals.
Hazor will be a desolation forever.
No person will live there.
No human will stay there.
passages.original: וְהָיְתָ֨ה חָצ֜וֹר לִמְע֥וֹן תַּנִּ֛ים שְׁמָמָ֖ה עַד־ עוֹלָ֑ם לֹֽא־ יֵשֵׁ֥ב שָׁם֙ אִ֔ישׁ וְלֹֽא־ יָג֥וּר בָּ֖הּ בֶּן־ אָדָֽם׃ס

passages.text: This is the word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning Elam at the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Jeremiah.
Jeremiah was a prophet.
The LORD gave Jeremiah a message about Elam.
This happened at the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah.
Zedekiah was king of Judah.
passages.original: אֲשֶׁ֨ר הָיָ֧ה דְבַר־ יְהוָ֛ה אֶל־ יִרְמְיָ֥הוּ הַנָּבִ֖יא אֶל־ עֵילָ֑ם בְּרֵאשִׁ֗ית מַלְכ֛וּת צִדְקִיָּ֥ה מֶֽלֶךְ־ יְהוּדָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר׃

passages.text: This is what the LORD of Hosts says: “Behold, I will shatter Elam’s bow, the mainstay of their might.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts speaks.
The LORD of Hosts is the God who commands heavenly armies.
The LORD says, “Look.
I will break the bow of Elam.
Elam is a nation.
Their bow is their main weapon.
Their bow is the source of their strength.
I will destroy this strength.”
passages.original: כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת הִנְנִ֥י שֹׁבֵ֖ר אֶת־ קֶ֣שֶׁת עֵילָ֑ם רֵאשִׁ֖ית גְּבוּרָתָֽם׃

passages.text: I will bring the four winds against Elam from the four corners of the heavens, and I will scatter them to all these winds. There will not be a nation to which Elam’s exiles will not go.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Jeremiah the prophet about Elam.
This happened at the beginning of Zedekiah’s reign as king of Judah.
The LORD of Hosts said these words.
The LORD said, “I will bring four winds against Elam.
These winds will come from the four corners of the heavens.
I will scatter the people of Elam to all these winds.
Elam’s exiles will go to every nation.
There will not be a nation where Elam’s exiles do not go.”
passages.original: וְהֵבֵאתִ֨י אֶל־ עֵילָ֜ם אַרְבַּ֣ע רוּח֗וֹת מֵֽאַרְבַּע֙ קְצ֣וֹת הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וְזֵ֣רִתִ֔ים לְכֹ֖ל הָרֻח֣וֹת הָאֵ֑לֶּה וְלֹֽא־ יִהְיֶ֣ה הַגּ֔וֹי אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹֽא־ יָב֥וֹא שָׁ֖ם נִדְּחֵ֥י עוֹלָם׃

passages.text: So I will shatter Elam before their foes, before those who seek their lives. I will bring disaster upon them, even My fierce anger,” declares the LORD. “I will send out the sword after them until I finish them off.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Hosts.
The LORD speaks with authority.
The LORD will shatter Elam.
Elam is a nation.
The LORD will do this in front of Elam’s enemies.
The LORD will do this in front of those who want to kill Elam’s people.
The LORD will bring disaster on Elam.
The LORD will show His fierce anger against Elam.
The LORD will send the sword after Elam.
The LORD will keep sending the sword until Elam is finished.
passages.original: וְהַחְתַּתִּ֣י אֶת־ עֵ֠ילָם לִפְנֵ֨י אֹיְבֵיהֶ֜ם וְלִפְנֵ֣י׀ מְבַקְשֵׁ֣י נַפְשָׁ֗ם וְהֵבֵאתִ֨י עֲלֵיהֶ֧ם׀ רָעָ֛ה אֶת־ חֲר֥וֹן אַפִּ֖י נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֑ה וְשִׁלַּחְתִּ֤י אַֽחֲרֵיהֶם֙ אֶת־ הַחֶ֔רֶב עַ֥ד כַּלּוֹתִ֖י אוֹתָֽם׃

passages.text: I will set My throne in Elam, and destroy its king and officials,” declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD will set His throne in Elam.
The LORD will destroy the king of Elam.
The LORD will destroy the officials of Elam.
passages.original: וְשַׂמְתִּ֥י כִסְאִ֖י בְּעֵילָ֑ם וְהַאֲבַדְתִּ֥י מִשָּׁ֛ם מֶ֥לֶךְ וְשָׂרִ֖ים נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: “Yet in the last days, I will restore Elam from captivity,” declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD promises restoration.
Elam is a nation.
Elam will go into captivity.
In the last days, the LORD will act.
The LORD will bring Elam back from captivity.
The LORD declares this.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֣ה׀ בְּאַחֲרִ֣ית הַיָּמִ֗ים אָשׁוּב אֶת־ שְׁבִית עֵילָ֖ם נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃ס
